title: Distributional systems and entropy flux pairs

items.title: Locally integrable functions define distributions
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; local prerequisite item; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb C)$. The regular functional $T_f$ defined by
$$\langle T_f,\varphi\rangle=\int_\Omega f(x)\varphi(x)\,dx\qquad(\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega))$$
is a distribution on $\Omega$ with the LF test-function topology.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis, lecture notes, Chapter 7, Section 7.3

items.title: Distributional systems and entropy flux pairs
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d,m\in\mathbb N$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, and let $\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open and convex. Put $Q=I\times\Omega$. A first-order conservation system on $\mathcal O$ consists of fluxes $F_j\in C^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^m)$, $1\leq j\leq d$, and the equation
$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}F_j(U)=0.$$
A state field $U:Q\to\mathcal O$ is locally bounded if it is measurable and essentially bounded on every compact subset of $Q$. For an open set $Q$, $g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(Q)$ means $g$ is measurable and $\int_K|g|<\infty$ for every compact $K\subseteq Q$. Require also $U,F_1(U),\ldots,F_d(U)\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(Q;\mathbb R^m)$. These fields then define regular distributions componentwise. The conservation system holds in distributions on $Q$ when, for every real-valued $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Q;\mathbb R^m)$,
$$\int_Q\left(U\cdot\partial_t\varphi+\sum_{j=1}^dF_j(U)\cdot\partial_{x_j}\varphi\right)\,dx\,dt=0.$$
This is the test-function meaning of the displayed derivative equation, using the distributional derivative convention in the supplied mathematics. The pairing is bilinear, without complex conjugation.

For an initial-value problem on $(0,T)\times\Omega$, $T>0$, let $U_0:\Omega\to\mathcal O$ be measurable and locally integrable. Require integrability of the state and fluxes up to the initial boundary:
$$\int_0^\tau\!\!\int_K\left(|U|+\sum_{j=1}^d|F_j(U)|\right)\,dx\,dt<\infty\qquad(0<\tau<T,\ K\subseteq\Omega\text{ compact}).$$
This condition uses only positive-time values and does not assert a strong trace at $t=0$. A test function up to the initial boundary is the restriction of a smooth function defined on a neighborhood of $[0,T)\times\Omega$, with compact support in $[0,T)\times\Omega$; its value at $t=0$ need not vanish. The initial-value weak identity is
$$\int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega\left(U\cdot\partial_t\varphi+\sum_{j=1}^dF_j(U)\cdot\partial_{x_j}\varphi\right)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega U_0(x)\cdot\varphi(0,x)\,dx=0$$
for every such real vector test function. The stated integrability up to the initial boundary makes every term finite, including for tests nonzero at $t=0$; a weak solution with initial data $U_0$ must satisfy these integrability conditions and this identity for all such tests.

A convex entropy-flux pair for the system is a function $\eta\in C^2(\mathcal O;\mathbb R)$ that is convex on the convex state domain $\mathcal O$ and functions $q_j\in C^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R)$ satisfying
$$Dq_j(V)=D\eta(V)\,DF_j(V)\qquad(V\in\mathcal O,\ 1\leq j\leq d),$$
where convexity means $\eta((1-\theta)V+\theta W)\leq(1-\theta)\eta(V)+\theta\eta(W)$ for $V,W\in\mathcal O$ and $\theta\in[0,1]$, and $D\eta,Dq_j$ are row derivatives while $DF_j$ is the Jacobian matrix. For a state field $U$, require $\eta(U),q_1(U),\ldots,q_d(U)\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ before using their distributions. The entropy inequality on $Q$ means
$$\partial_t\eta(U)+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}q_j(U)\leq0,$$
with the sign convention that this holds exactly when
$$\int_Q\left(\eta(U)\,\partial_t\psi+\sum_{j=1}^dq_j(U)\,\partial_{x_j}\psi\right)\,dx\,dt\geq0$$
for every nonnegative $\psi\in C_c^\infty(Q)$. With initial data on $(0,T)\times\Omega$, require also
$$\int_0^\tau\!\!\int_K\left(|\eta(U)|+\sum_{j=1}^d|q_j(U)|\right)\,dx\,dt<\infty\qquad(0<\tau<T,\ K\subseteq\Omega\text{ compact})$$
and $\eta(U_0)\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. Use every nonnegative scalar test up to the initial boundary defined above and add $\int_\Omega\eta(U_0)\psi(0,x)\,dx$ to the entropy integral. These conditions make all terms finite even when the test is nonzero at $t=0$. A weak solution satisfying this inequality is entropy-admissible relative to that pair.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter III §3.2 and Chapter IV §§4.3–4.5
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §§2–3
Piotr Gwiazda, Martin Michálek, and Agnieszka Świerczewska-Gwiazda, A Note on Weak Solutions of Conservation Laws and Energy/Entropy Conservation, §1

items.title: Planar shocks and piecewise smooth traces
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be open, $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, $\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be the state domain of a conservation system, $n\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $|n|=1$, and $s\in\mathbb R$. The planar interface and its two open sides are
$$\Sigma=\{(t,x)\in I\times\Omega:n\cdot x-st=0\},\qquad Q^-=\{(t,x)\in I\times\Omega:n\cdot x-st<0\},\qquad Q^+=\{(t,x)\in I\times\Omega:n\cdot x-st>0\}.$$
A state field is piecewise $C^1$ across $\Sigma$ if on each side it is $C^1$ and, near every point of $\Sigma$, each side field is the restriction of a $C^1$ map from a neighborhood in $I\times\Omega$ into $\mathcal O$. The left and right traces $U_L,U_R:\Sigma\to\mathcal O$ are the restrictions of those extensions to $\Sigma$; they are independent of the chosen extensions because they agree with the same field on their respective open sides. For any state or flux quantity $G$ with these traces, define its jump by $[G]=G_R-G_L$. A planar shock profile is such a piecewise $C^1$ state field with its specified constant interface normal $n$ and speed $s$; the definition does not assert that it solves a conservation system.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter III §3.1 and Chapter IV §4.3
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §3

items.title: Vector Rankine–Hugoniot condition
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$).

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be open, $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, $\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open and convex, and $F_j\in C^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^m)$. Let $n\in\mathbb R^d$ have $|n|=1$, let $s\in\mathbb R$, and let $\Sigma=\{(t,x)\in I\times\Omega:n\cdot x=st\}$. Suppose $U$ is piecewise $C^1$ across $\Sigma$, satisfies $\partial_tU+\sum_j\partial_{x_j}(F_j(U))=0$ pointwise on both open sides, and $U,F_j(U)\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. With $[G]=G_R-G_L$, the distributional residual is
$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}F_j(U)=\left(\sum_{j=1}^dn_j[F_j(U)]-s[U]\right)\delta_\Sigma,$$
Here spatial plane measure means the pushforward of Lebesgue measure $\lambda_{d-1}$ by $z\mapsto Ez+stn$, where $E:\mathbb R^{d-1}\to n^\perp$ is any linear isometry onto $n^\perp$. Explicitly, $\langle A\delta_\Sigma,\varphi\rangle=\int_I\int_{\{z:Ez+stn\in\Omega\}}A(t,Ez+stn)\cdot\varphi(t,Ez+stn)\,d\lambda_{d-1}(z)\,dt$. For $d=1$, $\mathbb R^0=\{0\}$ and $\lambda_0(\{0\})=1$. This definition is independent of $E$ and specifies the normalization without Hausdorff-measure notation. Consequently, $U$ solves the conservation system in distributions if and only if
$$s[U]=\sum_{j=1}^dn_j[F_j(U)]\quad\text{at every point of }\Sigma.$$
This is a vector equality; no division by the vector jump is made.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter III §3.1 and Chapter IV §4.3
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §3

items.title: Entropy jump residual
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$).

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open and convex, and let $F_j\in C^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^m)$, $1\leq j\leq d$. Let $n\in\mathbb R^d$ have $|n|=1$, let $s\in\mathbb R$, and set $\Sigma=\{(t,x)\in I\times\Omega:n\cdot x=st\}$. Suppose $U$ is piecewise $C^1$ across $\Sigma$, satisfies $U_t+\sum_jDF_j(U)\partial_{x_j}U=0$ classically on each open side, and the state, flux, and entropy compositions are locally integrable. Let $\eta\in C^2(\mathcal O;\mathbb R)$ be convex and let $q_j\in C^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $Dq_j(V)=D\eta(V)DF_j(V)$ for every $V\in\mathcal O$. With $[G]=G_R-G_L$, the distributional entropy residual is
$$\partial_t\eta(U)+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}q_j(U)=\left(\sum_{j=1}^dn_j[q_j(U)]-s[\eta(U)]\right)\delta_\Sigma.$$
Here $\delta_\Sigma$ uses the plane measure defined in the vector jump-residual theorem: integrate in $t$ and in $z\in\mathbb R^{d-1}$ with $x=Ez+stn\in\Omega$, where $E:\mathbb R^{d-1}\to n^\perp$ is a linear isometry onto $n^\perp$, using Lebesgue measure $\lambda_{d-1}$ and singleton mass one when $d=1$. The entropy inequality $\partial_t\eta(U)+\sum_j\partial_{x_j}q_j(U)\leq0$ holds near the interface if and only if $\sum_jn_j[q_j(U)]-s[\eta(U)]\leq0$ at every interface point. Entropy admissibility is an additional condition; the conservation jump equality alone does not imply it.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter III §3.2 and Chapter IV §4.5
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §§2–3
Piotr Gwiazda, Martin Michálek, and Agnieszka Świerczewska-Gwiazda, A Note on Weak Solutions of Conservation Laws and Energy/Entropy Conservation, §1

items.title: Strict hyperbolicity and Lax shock pattern
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
For a one-dimensional system $U_t+\partial_xF(U)=0$ with $F\in C^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^m)$ on an open state domain $\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, the system is strictly hyperbolic at $V\in\mathcal O$ if the Jacobian $DF(V)$ has $m$ distinct real eigenvalues. Write them in increasing order as $\lambda_1(V)<\cdots<\lambda_m(V)$. For states $U_L,U_R\in\mathcal O$ and speed $s\in\mathbb R$ satisfying the Rankine–Hugoniot equality
$$F(U_R)-F(U_L)=s(U_R-U_L),$$
assume strict hyperbolicity at both states. The jump is a $k$-Lax shock, $1\leq k\leq m$, if
$$\lambda_k(U_R)<s<\lambda_k(U_L),$$
and also $\lambda_{k-1}(U_L)<s$ when $k>1$, and $s<\lambda_{k+1}(U_R)$ when $k<m$. The outer inequality is omitted at each endpoint $k=1$ or $k=m$.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter III §3.1 and Chapter VIII §8.3
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §3

items.title: Strictly convex scalar Riemann construction
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$).

Let $F\in C^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$. Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$. If $a\ne b$, assume $F''(z)>0$ for every $z$ in the closed interval with endpoints $a,b$. Set $u_0(x)=a$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=b$ for $x>0$; its value at $x=0$ is arbitrary. For $t>0$ define the following profile:

- If $a=b$, let $u(t,x)=a$.
- If $a>b$, let $s=(F(a)-F(b))/(a-b)$ and let $u(t,x)=a$ for $x<st$ and $u(t,x)=b$ for $x>st$; its value on $x=st$ is arbitrary.
- If $a<b$, let $u(t,x)=a$ for $x/t\leq F'(a)$, let $u(t,x)=(F'|_{[a,b]})^{-1}(x/t)$ for $F'(a)<x/t<F'(b)$, and let $u(t,x)=b$ for $x/t\geq F'(b)$.

For each $T>0$, $C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\mathbb R)$ denotes restrictions of smooth functions defined on a neighborhood of $[0,T)\times\mathbb R$ and having compact support in that half-open cylinder; such a test may be nonzero at $t=0$. For every $T>0$ and every real test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\mathbb R)$, the initial-value weak identity
$$\int_0^T\!\!\int_{\mathbb R}\left(u\varphi_t+F(u)\varphi_x\right)\,dx\,dt+\int_{\mathbb R}u_0(x)\varphi(0,x)\,dx=0$$
holds. For every convex $\eta\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ and $q\in C^1(\mathbb R)$ with $q'=\eta'F'$, and for every $k\in\mathbb R$ with $\eta_k(z)=|z-k|$ and $q_k(z)=\operatorname{sgn}(z-k)(F(z)-F(k))$, the initial entropy inequality
$$\int_0^T\!\!\int_{\mathbb R}\left(\eta(u)\varphi_t+q(u)\varphi_x\right)\,dx\,dt+\int_{\mathbb R}\eta(u_0(x))\varphi(0,x)\,dx\geq0$$
holds for each nonnegative test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\mathbb R)$. In the rarefaction case $a<b$, both inequalities are equalities. In the shock case $a>b$, the speed satisfies $F'(b)<s<F'(a)$, so the shock has the scalar Lax pattern.

The sign function is $1$ on positive numbers, $0$ at zero, and $-1$ on negative numbers. The statement concerns these exact Riemann profiles and makes no general existence or uniqueness claim.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapters IV §§4.3–4.5 and Chapter VIII §8.3
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §§2–3
Piotr Gwiazda, Martin Michálek, and Agnieszka Świerczewska-Gwiazda, A Note on Weak Solutions of Conservation Laws and Energy/Entropy Conservation, §1

items.title: Entropy inequality under an assumed viscous limit
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $T>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $F\in C^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^d)$, and let $\eta\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be convex. Let $q\in C^1(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^d)$ satisfy $q_j'(z)=\eta'(z)F_j'(z)$ for every $z\in\mathbb R$ and $1\leq j\leq d$. For each $\epsilon>0$, let $u^\epsilon:[0,T]\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$, with initial trace $u_0^\epsilon:=u^\epsilon(0,\cdot)$, and let $u:(0,T)\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $u_0:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $u^\epsilon$, $\partial_tu^\epsilon$, all first spatial derivatives, and all second spatial derivatives are continuous on $[0,T]\times K$ for every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$. Suppose $u^\epsilon$ solves
$$\partial_tu^\epsilon+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}F_j(u^\epsilon)=\epsilon\Delta u^\epsilon\quad\text{on }(0,T)\times\Omega,$$
Suppose $|u^\epsilon|,|u|\leq M$ almost everywhere for one finite $M$, $u^\epsilon\to u$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,T)\times\Omega)$, and $u_0^\epsilon\to u_0$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. Here $f_\epsilon\to f$ strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(X)$ means $\int_K|f_\epsilon-f|\,d\lambda\to0$ for every compact $K\subseteq X$, with Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ on $X$. Then, for every nonnegative real test $\psi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\Omega)$,
$$\int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega\left(\eta(u)\partial_t\psi+\sum_{j=1}^dq_j(u)\partial_{x_j}\psi\right)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega\eta(u_0(x))\psi(0,x)\,dx\geq0.$$
This is a conditional passage for any family satisfying the stated smoothness, bound, and convergence assumptions; it asserts neither existence nor compactness of such a family.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter IV §4.6
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §2

title: Distributional systems and entropy flux pairs — Examples

items.title: Burgers shock entropy and Lax speeds
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $T>0$, let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ with $a>b$, and set $F(z)=z^2/2$ and $s=(a+b)/2$. For $t>0$ define $u(t,x)=a$ for $x<st$ and $u(t,x)=b$ for $x>st$; assign any value at $x=st$. Let $u_0(x)=a$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=b$ for $x>0$, with an arbitrary value at $x=0$. Then $u$ satisfies the initial-value weak identity for $u_t+\partial_xF(u)=0$. For every convex $\eta\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ and every $q\in C^1(\mathbb R)$ with $q'=\eta'F'$, it satisfies the initial-value entropy inequality with the convention that the distributional entropy residual is nonpositive. It also satisfies every Kružkov inequality for $\eta_k(z)=|z-k|$ and $q_k(z)=\operatorname{sgn}(z-k)(F(z)-F(k))$, where $\operatorname{sgn}(0)=0$. Its shock speed obeys $F'(b)<s<F'(a)$.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter IV §§4.3–4.5
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §§2–3

items.title: Burgers centered rarefaction and trace
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $T>0$, let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ with $a<b$, and set $F(z)=z^2/2$. For $t>0$ define
$$u(t,x)=\begin{cases}a,&x\leq at,\\ x/t,&at<x<bt,\\ b,&x\geq bt.\end{cases}$$
Let $u_0(x)=a$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=b$ for $x>0$, with any value at $x=0$. Then $u$ is continuous for $t>0$, satisfies the initial-value weak identity for $u_t+\partial_xF(u)=0$, and satisfies with equality the initial entropy identity for every convex $\eta\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ with compatible flux $q'=\eta'F'$ and every Kružkov pair $\eta_k(z)=|z-k|$, $q_k(z)=\operatorname{sgn}(z-k)(F(z)-F(k))$, where $\operatorname{sgn}(0)=0$. For every compact interval $K\subset\mathbb R$ and $t>0$,
$$\int_K|u(t,x)-u_0(x)|\,dx\leq(b-a)(|a|+|b|)t,$$
so $u(t,\cdot)\to u_0$ strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$ as $t\downarrow0$.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter IV §§4.3–4.5
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §§2–3

items.title: Expansion shock fails entropy selection
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). The assertion that every weak jump satisfying Rankine–Hugoniot is entropy-admissible is false. For $T>0$, let $a<b$, $F(z)=z^2/2$, $s=(a+b)/2$, and set $u(t,x)=a$ for $x<st$ and $u(t,x)=b$ for $x>st$ on $(0,T)\times\mathbb R$, with arbitrary value on the shock line. Give it Riemann initial data $u_0(x)=a$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=b$ for $x>0$, with arbitrary value at zero. This expansion shock is a weak solution but violates the entropy inequality for the convex entropy $\eta(z)=z^2/2$ and compatible entropy flux $q(z)=z^3/3$. The strictly convex scalar Riemann theorem supplies an entropy-admissible centered fan for the same flux and initial data; no general uniqueness conclusion is asserted.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter IV §§4.4–4.5
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §§2–3

items.title: Point assignments do not alter weak jump
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The assertion that a pointwise value assigned on a shock plane determines its one-sided trace or weak jump is false. Let $d,m\geq1$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, let $\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open and convex, and let $F_j\in C^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^m)$ for $1\leq j\leq d$. Let $n\in\mathbb R^d$ be a unit vector, let $s\in\mathbb R$, put $Q=I\times\Omega$, and set $\Sigma=\{(t,x)\in Q:n\cdot x=st\}$. Suppose $U:Q\to\mathcal O$ is measurable, has piecewise $C^1$ side fields with $C^1$ extensions to the interface, and $U,F_1(U),\ldots,F_d(U)\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(Q)$. Let $\widetilde U:Q\to\mathcal O$ be any measurable field that agrees with $U$ off $\Sigma$. Then $\widetilde U$ and $F_j(\widetilde U)$ are locally integrable and define the same regular distributions as $U$ and $F_j(U)$; their distributional conservation residuals are equal. For every convex $\eta\in C^2(\mathcal O)$ and compatible $q_j\in C^1(\mathcal O)$ with $Dq_j=D\eta\,DF_j$ whose compositions $\eta(U),q_j(U)$ are locally integrable, the corresponding compositions for $\widetilde U$ are locally integrable and have the same regular distributions and entropy residual. The two fields have the same one-sided traces and jump. In particular, assigning a third state on the shock plane does not change its weak jump condition.

references.title: Constantine M. Dafermos, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws in Continuum Physics, 2nd ed., Chapter III §3.1 and Chapter IV §4.3
Lawrence C. Evans, Entropy and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter V §3
